plots.title: Training and unseen-example error
plots.description: Recorded batch error and its 200-step average, compared with saved-checkpoint error on all training examples and a fixed set of 20,000 unseen examples. Vertical axis uses a logarithmic scale.

plots.title: Gap between unseen and training examples
plots.description: Positive values mean the saved network has more error on the fixed unseen examples. The same examples are used at every checkpoint.

plots.title: Learning-rate schedule
plots.description: Reconstructed from the verified training settings: 0.003 for the first 4,000 steps, then a gradual decrease to 0.0003 at step 20,000. This value was not logged separately.

plots.title: Changes in each layer
plots.description: Straight-line distance between consecutive saved weight and offset values, divided by elapsed steps. This is checkpoint movement, not gradient size or the full distance traveled between checkpoints.

plots.title: Predicted versus correct elevation
plots.description: Final network predictions on the same 20,000 unseen examples. The dashed line marks exact agreement; color counts examples in each small cell on a logarithmic scale.

plots.title: Distribution of final errors
plots.description: All 20,000 unseen examples. Negative values are predictions that are too low; positive values are predictions that are too high.

methods.checkpoint_error_evaluation: Same fixed held-out examples for every saved state; computed after training.
methods.snapshot_timing: Intermediate recorded step numbers precede that update; x-axis uses completed updates (recorded step minus one). Final snapshot follows all 20,000 updates.
methods.history_timing: Batch RMSE is recorded before each update; plotted against completed updates starting at zero.
methods.learning_rate: Reconstructed from verified trainer configuration: .003, exponential decay after 20% of steps to .0003.
methods.weight_changes: Euclidean distance of weights and offsets between snapshots divided by completed-update interval; not gradients or optimizer update magnitudes.
